raw_segments.text: I dug my cellar in the side of a hill sloping to the south, where a woodchuck had formerly
dug his burrow, down through sumach and blackberry roots, and the lowest stain of vegetation,
six feet square by seven deep, to a fine sand where potatoes would not freeze in any winter.
The sides were left shelving, and not stoned, but the sun having never shone on them the
It was but two hours' work.
I took particular pleasure in this breaking of ground, for in almost all latitudes men
dig into the earth for an equable temperature.
Under the most splendid house in the city is still to be found the cellar where they
store their roots as of old, and long after the superstructure has disappeared posterity
remark its dent in the earth.
The house is still but a sort of porch at the entrance of a burrow.
